newsitem.title: SPAIN: TENNIS-MOYA RECOVERS CLAY FORM IN BARCELONA.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-MOYA RECOVERS CLAY FORM IN BARCELONA.

text.p: Carlos Moya regained the form that has lifted him to number eight in the world when he began his Barcelona Open bid with an impressive win over Francisco Clavet on Wednesday.
The 6-4 6-4 win avenged a defeat by his fellow Spaniard last week in Estoril, where the Australian Open finalist had been unexpectedly out-of-sorts on his preferred, clay surface.
"I don't know what happened to me last week ... I've been doing morning and afternoon training sessions since then," said Moya, who admitted to having fitness problems.
Clavet, the losing finalist in Estoril, failed to take his only opportunity after breaking Moya early in the second set.
The Spanish number one took consecutive breaks after eliminating his backhand errors and mixing some outstanding lobs and drop shots into his baseline game.
"I'm pleased not for the result, but for the way I played," said Moya, who added his confidence had been affected by the defeat in Estoril and Spain's surprise Davis Cup elimination by Italy.
"Since the Australian Open, I've only really felt good in one game, and I lost some fitness on the American Tour," he said.
Moya, seeded fourth, remains on course for a repeat of last year's semi-final with reigning champion Thomas Muster of Austria, who needed three sets to beat Renzo Furlan of Italy on Tuesday.
With eight seeds already out, the most significant obstacle in Moya's path to the semifinals could be Andrei Medvedev.
The Ukranian followed Tuesday's victory over Estoril winner Alex Corretja with a comprehensive 6-2 6-0 win over another Spaniard, Carlos Costa.

In the bottom half of the draw local favourites Felix Mantilla and Alberto Berasategui lined up a quarter-final meeting with straight-sets wins over Francis Roig and Australian Richard Fromberg respectively.
